title: A stored last result must not be shown as the current state after a restart
rule: When the UI turns a persisted record of an earlier operation (a last check, a last scan, a last sync) into a present-tense state ('Version x is available', 'Up to date'), only do so when live state from this session confirms it (the store has the offer, the check ran since start). A record survives restarts and installs, so on its own it can describe a world that no longer holds (the found version is now the running one). Show the record as history in the row's line, and give the title a neutral state. Test it by recording the outcome, simulating a restart where the live source offers nothing, and asserting the title does not claim the old outcome.
rationale: E57.7 (#697): the About status row said 'Version 0.1.1 is available.' on 0.1.1 itself after an install, because it read the persisted last-check 'found' outcome while the store was idle.
